main_text.p: cur non & hæc purè Arabica, ut Dominum Nysæ sonet ? Quo modo autem Nysa ab Arabibus olim scripta fuerit non habeo quod statuam. [illegible, ~4 letters] inter Arabiæ urbes recentioribus notas nondum reperi, ita appellatam Ægypti provinciam quandam refert Safioddinus, eandem quæ & [illegible, ~5 letters] audit, diversam tamen statuit Author libri [illegible, ~9 letters] & Pagos 21. tantum continere, cùm Samannud 128 contineat [illegible, ~5 letters] Nawas apud Safioddinum est [illegible, ~6 letters] i.e. E Castellis Yamani. apud AlFirauzabadium in Kamuso suo, reperimus [illegible, ~6 letters] seu Nowasiensis appellari, speciem quandam uvarum præstantissimarum in [illegible, ~5 letters] Sarah {*} qui teste Safioddino, Mentium Hejazi altissimus, uvis & sacchari cannis abundans) quæ tamen num à loco aliquo vel aliunde sic dictæ, nihil monet. Inter Reges Yamanenses unum habuimus nomine [illegible, ~4 letters] Dy Nowas, quod si Διονυσ[?] Græcè efferatur propiùs aberit à sono, quam quæ ab una in alteram istarum linguarum translata sunt, non pauca. Sed ne incerta sectemur, cum ab omnibus pro concesso habeatur Nysam Arabiæ urbem fuisse in qua educatus à Nymphis Bacchus, olim notam licet nobis jam incognitam, atque ab ea denominari cum quod ad posteriorem nominis partem magnis Authoribus placeat, quod contenderim hoc est, non minùs probabiliter priorem ejus partem Arabum [illegible, ~3 letters] Du, vel in id obliquo [illegible, ~2 letters], statui. sed qui Arabibus debet ut Nysæ Dominus audiat unde Βάκχος[?] nuncupatus ? si ab incondita Bacchantium vociferatione, ut Eustathio placet, annon & hic Arabissantes ejus cultores habeamus judicent, qui audierint [illegible, ~6 letters] Bacche Bacche quod plane est.
{*} Num.fors. is qui apud Stephanum Byzantium. Ἀκουρῆς[?], ἡ κοπῆ[?] λεις ἡ καρων[?] ὐ[?] ἡ λόπολις τῆς Ἀξαβίας[?]

page.notes: Left margin note, lines 1–8: the Latin is printed in small italic type; the Greek lines at the foot of the margin are very small and only partly legible, so the Greek reading is doubtful throughout. The Arabic script in the text (several words, and the phrases at the end of the paragraph) is not legible enough to copy letter by letter; each is marked with an approximate letter count. The Greek word in the text after "Nysæ" (printed as Διόνυσ with a worn final letter) and the Greek word before "nuncupatus" (Βάκχος) are uncertain and marked [?]. The reference mark is a single asterisk after "Sarah" in the text, matching the note beginning "* Num.". The catchword "'Evôi" is at the bottom right.
